paragraphs: The day's rhythm is drawing, testing, and production follow-up. In the morning, revise CAD drawings according to engineer feedback and verify tolerances and standard parts. In the afternoon, assemble prototypes at the test bench, run tests, and copy the data for organization and analysis. When assembly issues arise in the workshop, go to the site, compare drawings with physical products, and finish and submit the test report in the evening.

In short, they turn engineers' ideas into physical products that can be drawn, assembled, and tested successfully. Work includes CAD drafting, prototype assembly and testing, data acquisition and analysis, process-document preparation, and on-site technical support.

AI rapidly takes over rules-based work such as drawing, annotation, and component selection, clearly reducing the value of traditional technician skills. At the same time, AI can double technician output, increasing demand for people who use it well. This is a role undergoing wholesale skill renewal.

Medium-to-high exposure is both a warning and an opportunity. Master AI drawing and simulation tools while strengthening process and on-site skills. Moving from drafter to a combined process + testing technician creates a stronger position during the AI transition.

Mechanical majors remain viable, but choose industries carefully. High-growth sectors such as new-energy vehicles, semiconductor equipment, and aerospace need technicians.
